title: Friendship Property
content: The friendship property states that every pair of distinct vertices has exactly one common neighbor. This captures the sociological intuition: any two people have exactly one mutual friend.
mathContext: $\text{IsFriendshipGraph}(G) \Leftrightarrow \forall u \neq v,\, |N(u) \cap N(v)| = 1$; in Lean: `IsFriendshipGraph G := ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (G.commonNeighbors u v).ncard = 1`. The common neighbor set is always a singleton under this condition.

title: Universal Vertex (Politician)
content: A universal vertex, also called a 'politician', is adjacent to every other vertex in the graph. The Friendship Theorem proves that every friendship graph must have such a vertex.
mathContext: `IsUniversalVertex G c := ∀ v ≠ c, G.Adj c v`; in degree terms: $\deg(c) = |V| - 1$. The universal vertex is characterized by having maximum possible degree in a simple graph on $|V|$ vertices.

title: Key Lemmas: Degree Constraints in Friendship Graphs
content:
Three lemmas constraining vertex degrees. `friendship_positive_degree`: every vertex has positive degree (since $n \geq 2$, each vertex has a common neighbor with some other vertex). `friendship_noncentral_degree`: non-center vertices have degree exactly 2 (adjacent only to the center and one partner). `universal_degree`: the center vertex has degree $n-1$ (adjacent to all others).

These degree constraints yield the handshaking identity $\sum \deg(v) = 3(n-1)$, which forces $n$ to be odd.
mathContext: In a friendship graph with universal vertex $c$: $\deg(c) = n-1$, $\deg(v) = 2$ for $v \neq c$. Sum: $(n-1) + 2(n-1) = 3(n-1)$. By handshaking: $2|E| = 3(n-1)$, so $2 \mid (n-1)$, hence $n$ is odd.

title: The Dichotomy: Universal Vertex or Regular Graph
content:
`friendship_has_universal_or_regular` establishes the key structural dichotomy: a friendship graph either has a universal vertex (done), or it is regular. The proof delegates to `FriendshipTheoremOQ01` which uses the $A^3$ commutativity argument — non-adjacent vertices must have the same degree.

`friendship_regular_implies_universal` then rules out the regular case via spectral analysis: the eigenvalue constraints of a regular friendship graph force the existence of a universal vertex.
mathContext: The adjacency matrix satisfies $A^2 = J - I + (k-1)A$ where $k$ is the common degree. Eigenvalue analysis: $\lambda^2 = n - 1 + (k-1)\lambda$, and the constraint $n = k^2 - k + 1$ combined with integrality forces $k \leq 2$.

title: Friendship Graphs Have Odd Order
content:
`friendship_card_odd` proves that every friendship graph has an odd number of vertices. The proof uses the degree constraints: with universal vertex $c$, $\deg(c) = n-1$ and $\deg(v) = 2$ for $v \neq c$, giving $\sum \deg(v) = (n-1) + 2(n-1) = 3(n-1)$. By handshaking $2|E| = 3(n-1)$, so $2 \mid (n-1)$, hence $n$ is odd.

`friendship_graph_is_windmill` then shows the converse direction: every friendship graph IS a windmill, completing the characterization.
mathContext: $|V| = 2k+1$ (odd). The windmill $W_k$ has $2k+1$ vertices, $3k$ edges, and $k$ triangles. The characterization: friendship graph $\iff$ windmill graph.

title: Windmill Graph Structure
content: A windmill graph (Dutch windmill) $W_n$ consists of $n$ triangles all sharing a common central vertex $c$. The definition requires: (1) $c$ is universal, and (2) non-central vertices are only connected through $c$ — for distinct non-central $u, v$ with $u \not\sim v$, their only common neighbor is $c$.
mathContext: `IsWindmillGraph G := ∃ c, IsUniversalVertex G c ∧ ∀ u v ≠ c, u ≠ v → ¬Adj u v → commonNeighbors u v = {c}`; $W_n$ has $2n+1$ vertices and $3n$ edges; $|V(W_n)| = 2n+1$ must be odd, a fact derivable from the friendship property.

title: The Friendship Theorem
content: The main result: every finite simple graph satisfying the friendship property has a universal vertex. This means someone must be friends with everyone.
mathContext: `friendship_theorem`: `IsFriendshipGraph G → Fintype.card V ≥ 3 → ∃ c, IsUniversalVertex G c`; proved via the spectral sandwich: either all vertices are regular (proved impossible for $|V| \geq 3$ unless universal vertex exists) or one vertex already has degree $|V|-1$.

title: Windmill Graph W₂
content: The windmill graph W₂ consists of two triangles sharing a common vertex (vertex 0). This is the simplest non-trivial friendship graph with 5 vertices.
mathContext: `windmill2 : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)` with vertex 0 as the universal vertex; adjacency defined by: 0∼1, 0∼2, 0∼3, 0∼4, 1∼2, 3∼4. Lemmas `windmill2_has_universal` and `windmill2_is_friendship` verify the friendship property holds.
